note: Curated context for /trials. 'watch' entries are hand-written; 'promising' tiers point at data/treatments.json ids. Edit here, not in trials.json, so a trials rebuild does not wipe it.

promising.blurb: Each has at least one randomised trial with a benefit on its main outcome. None is replicated in a large blinded ME/CFS trial, and the effects are modest.

promising.tier: Early signals with a controlled trial now running
promising.blurb: Uncontrolled or retrospective results that look large. Their placebo-controlled trials are the readouts most likely to change practice.
Worth knowing before anyone spends money on them. A failed trial in one population does not rule out a subgroup, but the burden of proof has moved.

ISRCTN74088209.why: Almost certainly amifampridine, which makes each nerve impulse release more acetylcholine, including at the autonomic ganglia that tighten veins. That is the pyridostigmine idea (steps 2-3) by a stronger route. No prior data in ME/CFS.
ISRCTN74088209.pos: Replicate in a larger parallel trial with standing haemodynamics measured. If symptoms improve without any change in circulation, it points at nerve-to-muscle or central cholinergic signalling, which the model leaves out.
ISRCTN74088209.neg: Weakens the case for boosting cholinergic transmission generally, though 2-week periods are short.
ISRCTN74088209.name: ReMEdi: PHOE-01 (amifampridine)

NCT06366724.why: The only placebo-controlled test of pyridostigmine over weeks rather than a single dose, crossed with low-dose naltrexone, and with an objective exercise outcome. Tests steps 3 and 5 directly.
NCT06366724.pos: Pyridostigmine moves from 'ask your doctor' to a standard trial for people with orthostatic intolerance; invasive CPET to find preload failure becomes worth doing.
NCT06366724.neg: The single-dose result was a physiology effect that does not carry over to daily life; the preload arm of the model would need another lever (volume, compression).
NCT06366724.name: LIFT: pyridostigmine and low-dose naltrexone

NCT07128082.why: 1,000-person blinded trial of tirzepatide for long COVID fatigue, run remotely with wearables. GLP-1 drugs have anti-inflammatory and central effects (steps 6-7) and a lot of patient anecdote, but no controlled data in ME/CFS.
NCT07128082.pos: First large positive drug trial in long COVID; would prompt an ME/CFS trial and a look at who responds (weight, inflammation markers).
NCT07128082.neg: Anecdotal benefit was weight loss or expectation; drop GLP-1 drugs from the ME/CFS shortlist.
NCT07128082.name: LOCITT: tirzepatide

NCT07280572.why: 1,250-person trial of metformin plus colchicine, two drugs that have each failed alone in established long COVID. Unblinded (vs usual care) with a self-rated outcome, so a benefit would need confirming.
NCT07280572.pos: Check whether the effect survives in the blinded subgroups or objective outcomes before acting on it.
NCT07280572.name: RECLAIM (UK): metformin and colchicine

NCT06631287.why: 550-person blinded trial of baricitinib, a JAK inhibitor, with an objective cognitive test as the main outcome. Tests whether ongoing interferon or cytokine signalling (steps 6-7) drives long COVID brain fog.
NCT06631287.pos: Strong evidence for an active inflammatory process in long COVID cognition; makes a JAK inhibitor trial in ME/CFS the obvious next step.
NCT06631287.neg: Argues against ongoing JAK-STAT cytokine signalling as the driver of cognitive symptoms.
NCT06631287.name: REVERSE-LC: baricitinib

NCT05513560.why: 460-person blinded trial (RECLAIM) of pentoxifylline, an old drug that improves red-cell flexibility and microcirculation (step 4), alongside an ibudilast arm aimed at glial inflammation (step 7).
NCT05513560.pos: First blinded support for a cheap, widely available microcirculation or anti-glial drug; the arm that wins says which step.
NCT05513560.neg: Another blow to the 'sticky blood / microclot' branch after the rivaroxaban null.
NCT05513560.name: RECLAIM: pentoxifylline and ibudilast

NCT06974084.why: 252-person blinded trial of maraviroc (a CCR5 blocker) plus atorvastatin, a combination promoted on the theory of persistent activated monocytes (steps 1 and 6) and already prescribed privately. Not yet recruiting.
NCT06974084.pos: Supports the monocyte persistence idea and gives the private-clinic regimen a basis.
NCT06974084.neg: Removes the evidence base from a regimen many patients are already paying for.
NCT06974084.name: IMPACT-LC: maraviroc and atorvastatin

NCT07359482.why: Replication of the 399-person Brazilian trial that found less fatigue with fluvoxamine. Fluvoxamine acts on sigma-1 receptors and inflammation as well as serotonin (steps 6-7).
NCT07359482.pos: Two positive blinded trials would make fluvoxamine the best-evidenced drug in long COVID.
NCT07359482.neg: The first result was chance or site-specific; demote it.
NCT07359482.name: ESPRIT: fluvoxamine

NCT07714213.why: The first placebo-controlled test of low-dose aripiprazole (138 people, crossover, Charité). The only data so far are a retrospective clinic review with no control group.
NCT07714213.pos: Moves aripiprazole from anecdote to evidence, and supports a dopamine or microglial component of the sickness response (step 7).
NCT07714213.neg: The clinic results were placebo and selection; drop it.
NCT07714213.name: PAIS-AriSE: low-dose aripiprazole

2024-520094-13-00.why: The randomised placebo-controlled follow-up (66 people, Haukeland) to the open-label pilot where 6 of 10 women improved markedly. Tests whether long-lived plasma cells and their antibodies keep the illness going (step 1).
2024-520094-13-00.pos: The strongest evidence yet for an antibody-driven subgroup; NK-cell count could be used to select patients.
2024-520094-13-00.neg: After rituximab, a second failure of B-lineage depletion would make an antibody cause much less likely.
2024-520094-13-00.name: ResetME: daratumumab

NCT06305793.why: 200-person blinded RECOVER-AUTONOMIC arm testing IVIG for long COVID POTS. Tests whether autoantibodies drive the autonomic symptoms (steps 1-2).
NCT06305793.pos: Supports an autoimmune form of post-COVID POTS; patient selection by autoantibody would be next.
NCT06305793.neg: Together with the efgartigimod and immunoadsorption nulls, the autoantibody explanation for POTS weakens considerably.
NCT06305793.name: RECOVER-AUTONOMIC: IVIG

NCT04740736.why: 106-person blinded trial of saline vs placebo infusion in ME/CFS, measuring blood volume and exercise testing. The direct test of step 3 driving step 5.
NCT04740736.pos: Supports low blood volume as a cause of the exercise limit; volume expansion becomes a treatment worth testing for crash prevention.
NCT04740736.neg: The 'would be disproved if' test for step 3: low volume explains orthostatic symptoms but not exercise intolerance.
NCT04740736.name: IV saline vs placebo infusion

NCT05697640.why: 104-person blinded trial of vericiguat, which restores nitric-oxide signalling in vessel walls, in post-COVID ME/CFS defined by Canadian criteria with PEM. A direct test of endothelial dysfunction (step 4).
NCT05697640.pos: First drug evidence that the vessel step matters; a mechanism-led target.
NCT05697640.neg: Endothelial dysfunction may be real but not limiting.
NCT05697640.name: Vericiguat

NCT07621068.why: 74-person sham-controlled trial of 60 sessions of hyperbaric oxygen in ME/CFS (Shamir, Israel), with exercise testing as the outcome. The ME/CFS test of the one positive long COVID sham trial.
NCT07621068.pos: Hyperbaric oxygen becomes a serious option, though expensive and travel-heavy for severe patients.
NCT07621068.neg: With HOT-LoCO negative, hyperbaric oxygen would be off the list.
NCT07621068.name: Hyperbaric oxygen in ME/CFS (Shamir)

NCT06960928.why: 80-person placebo-controlled trial of low-dose sirolimus (Mount Sinai). The uncontrolled study reported 74% improved; this is the first control group.
NCT06960928.pos: Supports immune or mTOR-driven persistence (steps 1, 6) and a cheap repurposed drug.
NCT06960928.neg: The open-label result was expectation; drop it.
NCT06960928.name: Sirolimus (Mount Sinai)

NCT07298005.why: 80-person blinded trial of sonlicromanol, a mitochondrial redox modulator developed for mitochondrial disease, targeting post-exertional malaise (steps 5-6).
NCT07298005.pos: First drug evidence that a cellular energy defect contributes to PEM.
NCT07298005.neg: Adds to the run of null mitochondrial supplements.
NCT07298005.name: SON4PEM: sonlicromanol

NCT07724834.why: 38-person blinded trial of inebilizumab, which depletes CD19 B cells and some plasmablasts, wider than rituximab. Tests the antibody hypothesis (step 1) from another angle.
NCT07724834.pos: Small, so a positive would need replication, but would revive B-cell therapy after rituximab.
NCT07724834.neg: Little added: too small to settle it.
NCT07724834.name: PIONEER: inebilizumab

NCT07316127.why: 70-person sham-controlled immunoadsorption trial in long COVID. Two sham trials are already negative.
NCT07316127.pos: Would conflict with the earlier sham trials; look at differences in patient selection.
NCT07316127.neg: Closes the question for unselected patients.
NCT07316127.name: Immunoadsorption vs sham

NCT06643299.why: 194-person blinded trial of a probiotic (PURE-LC), now completed. Gut dysbiosis and low indolepropionate replicate in four cohorts, so the gut difference is real; whether it is causal is open (step 1).
NCT06643299.pos: First controlled evidence that changing the microbiome changes symptoms.
NCT06643299.neg: Gut differences may be a consequence of illness and inactivity.
NCT06643299.name: PURE-LC: probiotic

NCT07597902.why: 150-person blinded factorial trial of valacyclovir, nirmatrelvir (Paxlovid) and celecoxib. Tests reactivated herpesvirus and persistent SARS-CoV-2 (step 1) in the same people.
NCT07597902.pos: Supports viral persistence or reactivation; the factorial design should say which drug carries it.
NCT07597902.neg: Adds to the nirmatrelvir nulls and weakens the herpes reactivation idea.
NCT07597902.name: SHIELD: valacyclovir, Paxlovid, celecoxib

NCT07916259.why: 1,300 young people, phase 3, blinded. Low-dose naltrexone failed in the 160-person adult trial, so this is now a test of whether younger people respond differently.
NCT07916259.pos: LDN gains its first strong evidence, in a younger population.
NCT07916259.neg: LDN would be very hard to justify at all.
NCT07916259.name: Brave-LC: low-dose naltrexone in young people

NCT04542161.why: 95-person blinded dose-response trial of N-acetylcysteine in ME/CFS, enrolling only people with low glutathione at baseline. One of few trials that selects patients by a measured abnormality.
NCT04542161.pos: A biomarker-selected treatment, and support for oxidative stress in the brain.
NCT04542161.neg: Low brain glutathione is a marker, not a cause.
NCT04542161.name: N-acetylcysteine in ME/CFS

NCT06305806.why: RECOVER-AUTONOMIC ivabradine arm (181). Reported at a conference: standing heart rate fell, symptoms did not.
NCT06305806.pos: Already reported at a meeting. The full paper may show a subgroup that benefits.
NCT06305806.neg: The fast heart rate is a compensation, not the problem: consistent with step 3 coming before step 8.
NCT06305806.name: RECOVER-AUTONOMIC: ivabradine
